$comment: Path-matched review rule packs, inspired by alibaba/open-code-review system_rules.json (Apache-2.0). Resolution: for each in-scope file, walk layers in priority order — (1) project <repo>/.reviewrules/manifest.json, (2) user ~/.claude/review-rules/manifest.json, (3) this built-in manifest. Within a layer, entries are evaluated top-to-bottom and the FIRST matching glob wins; once a layer matches, lower layers are not consulted for that file. Patterns support ** recursive match and {a,b} brace expansion. Doc paths are relative to the manifest's own directory. `scripts/resolve-rules.cjs` performs this resolution mechanically (2.1.0). The `risk` list uses the same layering to decide a file's review tier: `deep` means the change touches a domain the user's review policy escalates beyond /review-branch (code-audit-rigor skill + an exploitability-criteria security scan). These are path heuristics — a project ships its own `risk` list in .reviewrules/manifest.json to override them, and a project entry wins even when it says standard. Since 2.1.1 `resolve-rules.cjs --base <rev>` reads the whole project layer from that revision and does not parse the work tree's manifest (the reviewed branch cannot lower its own tier or remap its files; its own changes apply once merged), flags project rule docs the branch touched (`docsChanged`), and without --base bounds the work tree's manifest (size, entries, pattern length, brace expansions, work budget) with every problem a warning, not an error.
